reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) describes rapid heat-cool methods that suppress phase separation by non-equilibrium processing, but neither passage provides any data or discussion on the effect of a controlled dwell at a critical nucleation temperature, near-equilibrium nucleation, or in situ optimization of dwell time. The key premises about dwell-enhanced diffusion and controlled nucleation are therefore unsupported by the cited prior work.
premises: A dwell at a critical nucleation temperature can enhance uniform atomic diffusion and homogenization of noble metal precursors
Controlled nucleation under near-equilibrium conditions promotes single-phase FCC formation
Rapid heat-cool synthesis without a dwell leads to uncontrolled nucleation, phase separation, and elemental segregation
The mechanism applies at temperatures just below the precursor decomposition threshold
In situ monitoring can identify an optimal dwell time to avoid coarsening or unwanted phase transitions
